reader.requirement: At --std 85 an input-output statement on a sequential file that fails with a permanent error (status 30, 34, 35, 37, 38, 39) is unsuccessful, any applicable USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure runs (by file-name or by open-mode phrase), and once the condition arises on a file it stays in effect for every later input-output operation on that file until an implementor-defined correction technique is applied.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.CloseWithLockLocksFileConnector: at 85 a CLOSE WITH LOCK locks the PHYSICAL file (any SELECT of it then gets 38), from 2002 only the file connector
the same behavior on the OPEN side: physical-file lock at 85, connector lock from 2002
DialectBehavior.FileSharingFacility (from 2002): at 85 an OPEN refused by a sharing conflict reports the permanent error 30 instead of 61

reader.edition-search: grep for DialectBehaviors.IsActive, Edition, CobolVersion and DialectLevel in Runtime/IO/*.cs and in CodeGen DispatchEmitter/EcEmitter/UseTierEmitter/SequentialIoEmitter; the permanent-error record and replay (FileConnector#Status setter, PermanentErrorReplay) consult no edition and are the code every edition takes
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 the 38 of a CLOSE WITH LOCK applies to the physical file through every file-name (from 2002, to the connector only), and with no sharing facility at 85 a sharing refusal on OPEN is 30; the persistence and the USE dispatch are the same at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f15_01 exercises 38 and 35 with a USE procedure; it does not witness the persistence sentence on an open connector, nor USE by open-mode phrase (INPUT, I-O, EXTEND), nor the 85 physical-file lock through a second SELECT

probes.expected: 35 for OPEN INPUT, I-O and EXTEND of a missing non-optional file, each running the USE declarative of that open mode (§1985:VII.4.6.4 GR5b); 38 for OPEN of the physical file through a second SELECT after CLOSE WITH LOCK through the first

probes.printed: E 38 (second SELECT FD2 of the file closed WITH LOCK through FD1)
probes.expected: the 85 meaning of 'a file previously closed with lock' is the physical file

reader.notes: The permanent error is recorded at the one Status setter whenever a 3x status lands on an OPEN connector and replayed by every verb's precondition; CLOSE is the documented implementor-defined correction (docs/conformance DOC-A.1-105), so a failed OPEN (connector stays closed) is already corrected and a repeated OPEN meets the condition afresh. The persistence was probed with the deterministic ODO READ 34; host failures 30 and boundary 34 on WRITE share the same setter but cannot be raised deterministically here. Continuing after the USE procedure for a critical status is the implementor's choice (§1985:VII.4.6.4 GR6).

refuter.evidence: Read FileConnector#Status setter (records a 3x on an open connector), #PermanentErrorReplay and docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-105.md (CLOSE is the documented implementor-defined correction; a failed OPEN leaves the connector closed = corrected). ON INPUT; CLOSE 00; OPEN I-O 00, READ 34, REWRITE 34, READ 34 each running USE ... ON I-O; USES 08. cite.py: OK §1985:VII.1.3.5 GR3 (the text is in GR3).
